_comment: Three hooks plus two allow rules. UserPromptSubmit reprints a one-line reminder about the user-level CLAUDE.md each turn, since CLAUDE.md loads once at session start and its guidance fades over a long session - confirmed in a real session (2026-09-22) to be a nudge the model reads past rather than one that changes behavior on its own; kept anyway since it's free (no extra round-trip) and covers the whole file, not just note-taking. Stop forces one explicit check against the notes repo before each turn ends, added because that nudge alone wasn't enough for the specific 'take notes proactively' instruction - it returns hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext rather than decision:block so Claude Code labels it 'Stop hook feedback' in the transcript rather than a hook error (nothing is wrong when it fires, it's a routine checkpoint), and it checks stop_hook_active to avoid looping (Claude Code also hard-caps at 8 consecutive blocks regardless). Commit review is no longer a hook: the PreToolUse agent hook that reviewed each git commit (2026-10-21) was replaced by a CLAUDE.md instruction to run the commit-reviewer subagent (claude/agents/commit-reviewer.md) before committing, because a passed agent-hook review left no trace anywhere, while a subagent's verdict shows in the session. PostToolUse on Bash, narrowed with 'if': 'Bash(gh *)', runs pr-review-nudge.sh. The 'if' names only the command because a pattern that names arguments, like 'Bash(gh pr create*)', runs the hook anyway on any command containing $(), backticks or $VAR (hooks reference), which after install meant most Bash calls. The script then reads stdin with jq and nudges only when the command mentions 'pr create' and its output has a .../pull/<number> URL, and exits silently without jq. It returns fixed additionalContext reminding the agent of the CLAUDE.md 'Review after opening a PR' step: run /code-review on the PR, then ask the user whether to post the findings on the PR or fix them locally. It only reminds; the review and the question are the agent's. The permissions block allows the reviewer's two commands, the user-messages.sh helper and git diff: in an auto-mode session (2026-10-21) the reviewer's ad-hoc jq on the transcript and git diff --cached were refused, so it reviewed blind. The jq filter lives in a script so the rule can stay that narrow. Rules use a literal ~ because Bash rules match the command text as typed and the reviewer's prompt tells it to type ~. The install-claude skill merges this 'hooks' block into ~/.claude/settings.json, adds this permissions.allow list to the one in ~/.claude/settings.json, and copies each claude/hooks/*.sh into ~/.claude/hooks/. Commands use $HOME because a machine-specific absolute path can't be committed here; ~ never expands in hook command strings, and $HOME expands only if the harness runs the command through a shell rather than exec'ing it directly, so the skill rewrites this to an absolute path on machines where $HOME stays literal.
